mainTopic: Rights of passage and use on someone else's land: inner gardens, water channels and their banks, and moving a public road
overview: The amud opens with the last words of the previous discussion: the homeowner may put his own lock on the door because of a concern about his wife. A new משנה follows. Someone whose garden can only be reached through his חבר's garden may pass only at normal hours, may not bring in תגרין, and may not use it as a shortcut, and the outer owner may plant on the path. If a side path was set up with both owners' agreement, he may come and go freely and bring תגרין, but nobody may plant on that path. The גמרא brings שמואל's rulings on how much land comes with a sold water channel and who may grow things on its banks. It then discusses whether the channel owner may repair collapsed banks with earth from the field, where רב פפא replaces שמואל's reason with a condition of the sale. A second משנה teaches that a man who moves a public road to the side of his field loses both roads, and it lists standard widths for paths and roads. The גמרא asks whether this proves a person may never enforce his own rights, and two answers in רבא's name show that it does not.

steps.title: The reason for the homeowner's lock: suspicion about his wife
steps.stepSummary: The previous discussion ends: the homeowner locks his door because of a possible suspicion about his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is because of suspicion regarding his wife.
steps.whatsHappening: These are the last words of the previous sugya, which asked why the owner of a house makes his own lock when someone else's בור is inside his house. The answer is the concern of חשד with his wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the owner of the בור could come in while the homeowner is away, he might end up alone in the house with the homeowner's wife. The homeowner's own lock prevents this, so he is entitled to it.

keyTerms.meaning: Suspicion; concern that something improper could happen or be suspected

phrases.english: Because of suspicion regarding his wife.
phrases.notes: This finishes the earlier question about why the homeowner puts his own lock on the door when a neighbor's pit is inside his house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the answer to a question from the previous section.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The homeowner's lock is justified because of the concern of seclusion with his wife.

steps.title: An inner garden reached through a neighbor's garden
steps.stepSummary: The משנה sets limits on someone who must pass through his חבר's garden to reach his own garden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone whose garden lies behind his friend's garden may go in and out only at normal hours. He may not bring merchants inside, and he may not use the garden as a passage into another field. The owner of the outer garden may plant on the path.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a garden that can only be reached by walking through someone else's garden. It lists what the inner owner may and may not do on the path.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inner owner has only a right of passage, so the outer owner is protected from disturbance: no odd hours, no crowds of תגרין, and no use as a shortcut to other fields. Because the path was never set aside, the outer owner may even plant on it, and the inner owner walks through the planted area.

keyTerms.meaning: The outer one (the owner of the outer garden)

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who has a garden
further inside than his fellow's garden –
phrases.notes: He means the only way to reach his garden is by walking through his friend's garden.

phrases.aramaic: נִכְנָס בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁדֶּרֶךְ בְּנֵי אָדָם נִכְנָסִים,
phrases.english: enters at a time when people usually enter,

phrases.aramaic: וְיוֹצֵא בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁדֶּרֶךְ בְּנֵי אָדָם יוֹצְאִין;
phrases.english: and leaves at a time when people usually leave;
and he may not bring merchants into it;
and he may not enter from it
into another field;
and the outer one may sow the path.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ גִּינָּה לִפְנִים מִגִּינָּתוֹ שֶׁל חֲבֵרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new case of access through another person's property.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An inner garden owner who passes through another's garden is limited to normal hours, no merchants, and no passage to other fields, and the outer owner may plant the path.

steps.title: A side path set up with both owners' agreement
steps.stepSummary: When a fixed side path was given with both owners' consent, the inner owner gets more freedom, but nobody may plant on the path.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he was given a path along the side with both of them agreeing, he may come and go whenever he wants and may bring merchants in. He still may not pass through his garden into another field. Neither of them may plant on that path.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה contrasts the first case with a second one, where a set path along the side was agreed to by both owners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the path is a fixed, defined strip, so passing through it no longer bothers the outer owner. That is why the time limits and the ban on merchants fall away. The shortcut ban stays, and because the path is now a real road, neither owner may plant on it.

keyTerms.meaning: With the agreement of both of them

steps.whatToRemember: An unfixed path through the middle gives limited rights, and the outer owner may plant it. A fixed side path agreed to by both gives full freedom of coming and going, and then nobody may plant it. In both cases, using the garden as a shortcut to another field is forbidden.

phrases.english: If they gave him a path from the side
with the agreement of both of them –
he enters at a time that he wants,
and leaves at a time that he wants;
and he may bring merchants into it.

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא יִכָּנֵס מִתּוֹכָהּ לְתוֹךְ שָׂדֶה אַחֶרֶת.
phrases.english: But he may not enter from it into another field.
Neither this one nor that one is permitted to sow it.
phrases.notes: Neither the inner garden's owner nor the outer garden's owner may plant on the side path.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָתְנוּ לוֹ דֶּרֶךְ מִן הַצַּד מִדַּעַת שְׁנֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a contrasting case to the first half of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With an agreed side path, the inner owner may come and go freely and bring merchants, but may not pass through to another field, and neither owner may plant the path.

steps.title: How much land comes with a sold water channel
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל: selling a channel for a בית השלחין includes 2 cubits for the channel and 1 cubit for each bank. A channel for a בית הקילון includes 1 cubit and half a cubit for each bank.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: If someone says "I am selling you a channel for an irrigated field," he must give two cubits for the inside of the channel and one cubit on each side for its banks. If he says "I am selling you a channel for a shadoof," he gives one cubit for the inside and half a cubit on each side for its banks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a statement from שמואל about the sale of a water channel through the seller's land. It defines exactly how wide a strip the buyer receives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A channel needs its banks to hold the water and to be maintained, so the sale automatically includes land on both sides. A large irrigation channel gets a wider strip. A small channel fed by a קילון, a bucket-lifting device, gets half of that.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: a water channel (in other places, a cubit)
An irrigated field that depends on watering
A field watered with a קילון, a pole-and-bucket device for lifting water

steps.confusionAlert: The word אמה appears here with two meanings. In "אמה בית השלחין" it means a water channel. In "שתי אמות" and "חצי אמה" it means a cubit, a unit of length.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
"I am selling you a channel for an irrigated field" –
phrases.notes: Here אמה means a water channel, not a cubit.

phrases.english: he gives him two cubits for its inside,
and a cubit on this side and a cubit on that side for its banks.
"I am selling you a shadoof channel" –
phrases.notes: A קילון is a pole with a bucket for lifting water, so its channel is smaller.

phrases.english: he gives him one cubit for its inside,

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲצִי אַמָּה מִכָּאן וַחֲצִי אַמָּה מִכָּאן לַאֲגַפֶּיהָ.
phrases.english: and half a cubit on this side and half a cubit on that side for its banks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins with a related rule about rights running through another person's land.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sold irrigation channel includes 2 cubits plus 1 cubit for each bank. A shadoof channel includes 1 cubit plus half a cubit for each bank.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets standard default measurements, so a sale of a channel has defined boundaries even when the seller did not spell them out.

steps.title: Who may sow the channel's banks?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who has the right to use the banks of the channel.
steps.simpleTranslation: And those banks, who may sow them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a practical follow-up to שמואל's measurements: who gets to use the strips of bank alongside the channel? This question sets up the next step, where the answer is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 taught that the channel owner gets extra ground for banks on each side. Now we need to know whether those banks are only for holding the channel, or whether the field owner may still grow things on them.

keyTerms.meaning: Banks; the strips of earth on both sides of the channel
Sows them with seeds (vegetables or grain)

phrases.english: And those banks, who sows them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks a follow-up question about the banks set aside in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the field owner or the channel owner may use the banks, and for what kind of growing.

steps.title: Two reports of שמואל: sow or plant
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל that the field owner sows the banks; רב נחמן quotes שמואל that the field owner plants trees on them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: the field owner sows them. רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל: the field owner plants them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with two different reports of what שמואל said. Both agree the field owner uses the banks, but they differ on how.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions agree the banks still belong to the field owner for growing things. The only difference is the kind of growing: seeds (זריעה) or trees (נטיעה).

keyTerms.meaning: The owner of the field the channel runs through

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The field owner sows them.
Rav Nachman said that Shmuel said:
The field owner plants them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: בַּעַל הַשָּׂדֶה זוֹרְעָם
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The field owner uses the banks; one version says he sows them, the other says he plants trees on them.

steps.title: Explaining the gap between the two versions
steps.stepSummary: Whoever allows sowing surely allows planting; whoever allows only planting forbids sowing because it loosens the soil.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says 'sows them' holds that all the more so he may plant them. The one who says 'plants them' holds he may not sow them, because sowing makes the soil loose and crumbly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains exactly how far apart the two versions of שמואל are. It shows that one view is more lenient and gives the reason for the stricter view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב יהודה, sowing is allowed, so planting trees is allowed with even more reason (כל שכן). According to רב נחמן, only trees are allowed, because sowing requires breaking up the soil, which weakens the banks and can damage the channel.

keyTerms.meaning: They make the ground loose and full of holes

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think trees are worse for the bank than seeds. Here the גמרא treats sowing as the bigger danger, because it loosens the soil.

phrases.english: The one who says "he sows them":
all the more so he may plant them.
And the one who says "he plants them":
but sowing them, no,
because they loosen the soil.
phrases.notes: Literally "they make holes." Sowing breaks up the earth, so the bank gets weaker and can crumble into the channel.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר זוֹרְעָם – כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן נוֹטְעָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the logic behind each of the two versions in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sowing is the more harmful use; whoever permits it surely permits trees, and whoever permits only trees forbids sowing because it loosens the soil.

steps.title: Fixing collapsed banks with the field's earth
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that if the channel's banks collapse, the channel owner may repair them using earth from the field, because the bank's earth fell only into that field.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: a water channel whose banks collapsed, he may fix it with earth from that field, because it is known that its banks collapsed only into that field.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling from שמואל: when the channel's banks fall apart, the channel owner may take earth from the surrounding field to rebuild them. The reason given is that the fallen earth surely landed in that field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The field belongs to someone else, so taking its earth needs a reason. שמואל's reason is that the channel owner is really just taking back his own earth, which slid into that field.

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
A water channel whose banks collapsed,
he repairs it from that field,
phrases.notes: He means he takes earth from the field around the channel, even though it isn't his field.

phrases.english: since it is known that its banks did not collapse
except into that field.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: אַמַּת הַמַּיִם שֶׁכָּלוּ אֲגַפֶּיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling of שמואל about the same channel, now about repairs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The channel owner may repair collapsed banks with earth from the field, because the bank's earth fell into that field.

steps.title: רב פפא: your water washed it away
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא objects: the field owner can say, your own water knocked down your banks, so why take my earth?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא objected: let the field owner say to him, your water washed your earth down; that is not my problem.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא attacks the reason שמואל gave. He argues the field owner has a good reply: the earth was lost because of the channel owner's own water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's reason depends on the claim that the fallen earth is sitting in that field. רב פפא disputes this: the field owner can say the channel's own water swept the bank's earth away down the channel, not into his field. So there is no proof that the field holds the channel owner's earth.

keyTerms.meaning: Washed it down / carried it away

phrases.english: Rav Pappa objected to this:
But let him say to him:
phrases.notes: The field owner is speaking to the channel owner.

phrases.english: Your water carried away your earth!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב פָּפָּא, וְלֵימָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's reason that the fallen earth is known to be in that field.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The field owner can claim the channel's water carried the bank's earth away, not into his field, so שמואל's premise that the earth is known to be in that field fails.

steps.title: A new reason: the field owner agreed to it
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the field owner accepted this condition when he sold the channel rights.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב פפא said: the reason is that the field owner accepted this upon himself as a condition.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא keeps שמואל's ruling but replaces the reason. The channel owner may take earth because the field owner agreed to it from the start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling stays the same, but it now rests on the deal, not on who owns the fallen earth. When the field owner sold the channel, it was understood that repairs could use earth from his field.
steps.whatToRemember: The channel owner may fix collapsed banks with the field's earth. According to רב פפא, this is because the field owner agreed to it when he sold the channel, not because the earth is the channel owner's.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Pappa said:
Because on that condition
the field owner accepted it upon himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: שֶׁעַל מְנָת כֵּן קִבֵּל עָלָיו בַּעַל הַשָּׂדֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's own objection by giving a new reason for the same ruling.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the reason while keeping the ruling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The channel owner may take earth because it is his own earth that fell into the field.
steps.terutzMaskana: The channel owner may take earth because the field owner agreed to it as a condition of the sale.

steps.title: New משנה: moving a public road to the side
steps.stepSummary: If a man moves a public road from inside his field to its edge, the new road becomes public, and he still does not get the old road.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: someone who had a public road passing through his field, and he took it and gave them a road on the side: what he gave, he gave, and his own he did not get.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens a new topic: a public road running through a private field. If the owner takes it and gives the public a road along the edge instead, he loses both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new road on the side now belongs to the public. The old road also stays public, so he loses both. The גמרא in steps 13–16 explains why he cannot take the old road back.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (marks the start of a new משנה)
Did not reach him; he does not get it

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who had a public road
passing through his field,
and he took it and gave them one on the side,
what he gave, he gave,
and his own did not reach him.
phrases.notes: "His own" is the old road he tried to take for himself. It stays public, so he does not get it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ מִי שֶׁהָיְתָה דֶּרֶךְ הָרַבִּים עוֹבֶרֶת לְתוֹךְ שָׂדֵהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic: a public road through a private field.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If he moves a public road to the side of his field, the new road is public and the old road still stays public.

steps.title: Standard sizes of paths, roads, and the mourners' standing place
steps.stepSummary: The משנה sets standard widths: a private path is four אמות, a public road is sixteen אמה, and the king's road and the road to a grave have no limit. The judges of ציפורי set the standing place for comforting mourners at a בית ארבעה קבין.
steps.simpleTranslation: A private path is four cubits wide. A public road is sixteen cubits wide. A king's road has no limit. A road to a grave has no limit. As for the standing place, the judges of Tzippori said: an area where four kav of seed are sown.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a list of standard sizes for different kinds of paths and gathering places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These sizes apply when someone sells or grants a path and does not say how wide it is. The king's road and the road to a grave have no set maximum, so no fixed width limits them. The standing place for mourners is measured as an area, not a width, following the ruling of the judges of ציפורי.

keyTerms.meaning: A private path used by one person
The place where people stand after a burial to comfort the mourners
An area big enough to sow four קַב of seed

phrases.english: A private path – four cubits.
A public road – sixteen cubits.
A king's road – it has no set measure.
A road to a grave – it has no set measure.
The standing place –
phrases.notes: After a burial, people would stand in rows to comfort the mourners. This is the size of that space.

phrases.english: The judges of Tzippori said:
An area for sowing four kav.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's rules about roads by listing the standard widths.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Private path 4 אמות; public road 16 אמה; king's road and grave road unlimited; standing place for mourners בית ארבעה קבין.

steps.title: Why can't he just guard the old road himself?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's ruling that the man who moved the public road does not get the old road. Since he gave the public a new road, let him take a stick and sit on the old road to keep people off.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does the משנה say his own did not reach him? Let him take a stick and sit there!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now opens its discussion and goes back to the case from step 11, asking why the man cannot simply claim the old road.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He gave the public a fair trade, so it seems the old road should be his. He could physically stop people from walking on it. So why does the משנה say he never gets it?

keyTerms.meaning: What is his did not reach him: he does not get the old road back

phrases.english: GEMARA
Why did his own not reach him?
phrases.notes: This quotes the end of the משנה from step 11: he moved the road, but the old road does not become his.

phrases.english: Let him take a stick and sit!
phrases.notes: He means: let him sit on the old road with a stick and keep people from walking through.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling stated in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the man who moved the road does not get the old road
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He gave the public an exchange, so he should be able to claim the old road and physically defend it.

steps.title: Does this prove a person may never enforce his own rights?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the משנה proves a person may not take the law into his own hands even when he will lose out. That would clash with the accepted rule that he may.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you learn from this that a person may not do justice for himself, even where there is a loss?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes the question further: if he cannot guard the old road, this seems to prove a big general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The accepted הלכה is that when a person stands to lose, he may act on his own to protect what is his. If the משנה forbids that here, it seems to contradict that rule. So the גמרא needs an explanation for why this case is different.

keyTerms.meaning: A person does justice for himself: enforcing his own rights without going to בית דין
Where there is a loss: when waiting would cost him
Can you learn from this? A formula for drawing a conclusion

phrases.english: Do you learn from this
that a person may not do justice for himself –
even where there is a loss?

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁמְעַתְּ מִינַּהּ לָא עָבֵיד אִינִישׁ דִּינָא לְנַפְשֵׁיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a troubling general conclusion from the question in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling, read as a general rule against self-help
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the משנה forbids self-help even when he will lose, it contradicts the accepted הלכה that a person may enforce his own rights to prevent a loss.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not deciding that self-help is forbidden. It is asking whether the משנה proves that, and the answers that follow show it does not.

steps.title: רב זביד: a special decree in case he gives a crooked road
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד in the name of רבא answers that self-help is normally allowed, but here the חכמים made a decree in case the man gives the public a winding road.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד said in the name of רבא: It is a decree, in case he gives them a crooked road.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer, which keeps the general rule of self-help in place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if his new road is just as good, the חכמים never let anyone keep the old road. They worried that people would come to swap a straight road for a winding one, making the public walk farther. So the ruling is a protective decree, not a rejection of self-help.

keyTerms.meaning: A decree the חכמים made to prevent a problem

phrases.english: Rav Zevid said in the name of Rava:
It is a decree,
in case he gives them a crooked road.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב זְבִיד מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא: גְּזֵירָה שֶׁמָּא יִתֵּן לָהֶן דֶּרֶךְ עֲקַלָּתוֹן
steps.terutzResolutionType: Special decree that sets this case apart from the general rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seems to forbid self-help even where there is a loss.
steps.terutzMaskana: Self-help is allowed in general. Here a decree applies even to a fair exchange, in case people give crooked roads.
steps.whyThisMatters: It keeps the general הלכה of עָבֵיד אִינִישׁ דִּינָא לְנַפְשֵׁיהּ in place.

steps.title: רב משרשיא: the משנה only means when he actually gives a crooked road
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא in the name of רבא answers differently: the משנה only speaks of a case where the man really gave the public a winding road. If the new road is just as straight, he may keep the old one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא said in the name of רבא: The משנה is talking about where he gives them a crooked road.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different answer, also in רבא's name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no decree here. The משנה is about a bad exchange, where the new road is winding, so the man has not really paid the public back. In a fair exchange for an equally straight road, he may take the old road, and self-help stays allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: In a case where he gives them

steps.whatToRemember: Both answers agree that a person may enforce his own rights to prevent a loss. They disagree on a fair exchange: רב זביד forbids taking the old road even then, because of a decree, while רב משרשיא allows it.

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiyya said in the name of Rava:
It is where he gives them a crooked road.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא אָמַר: בְּנוֹתֵן לָהֶם דֶּרֶךְ עֲקַלָּתוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer that disagrees with step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה forbids keeping the old road in every exchange.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה only applies when the new road is crooked. In a fair, straight exchange he may take the old road.
